episodes.label: The Ion That Rode Through the Membrane — Monensin Polyether Sodium Ionophore (US3501568), Electroneutral Na+/H+ Collapse & Secondary Ca2+ Overload, Equine vs. Cattle Species Sensitivity & Human Rhabdomyolysis
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 91: Monensin Polyether Sodium Ionophore (US3501568), Electroneutral Na+/H+ Collapse & Secondary Ca2+ Overload, Equine vs. Cattle Species Sensitivity & Human Rhabdomyolysis. A patient arrives weak, with aching thighs and brown urine. A veterinary product label changes what the team asks, but the first blood samples measure the damage already underway. The patient, clinical measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Meliton N. Novilla’s 2011 chapter “Ionophores,” which discusses monensin, coccidia, cattle and the consequences of altered sodium and calcium handling. Pharmacology notebook · Chapter 29

episodes.label: The Cat Hair in the Case — Feline Pocket-Lift mtDNA Replication (Lyons 2014), Snowball Nuclear STRs (1997), Maternal Household Relatives & Nanopore Mitogenomes/NUMTs
episodes.notes: Forensic animal genetics and maternal-lineage probability limits: Lyons et al.'s (2014) Missouri homicide feline pocket-hair mtDNA masked replication across household maternal relatives vs. Menotti-Raymond et al.'s (1997) Snowball 10-locus nuclear STR root match, Grahn et al.'s (2011, N=1,394) feline control-region database, and Patterson et al.'s (2023) 60-amplicon Nanopore whole-mitogenome sequencing and nuclear mitochondrial pseudogene (NUMT) traps.

episodes.label: The Jet That Hugged the Wall — Canine Eccentric Coandă Mitral Regurgitation Jets (V015), 2D vs. 3D Echocardiography, EPIC Chamber Cutoffs & Focused Echo Agreement
episodes.notes: One Medicine veterinary cardiology and Doppler physics (V015): Kanemoto et al.'s (2024) congenital mitral valve dysplasia puppy showing how wall-hugging Coandă jets underestimate regurgitant severity on 2D color-flow mapping, 3D echocardiographic vena contracta comparisons (2017), Boswood et al.'s (2016) EPIC trial LA:Ao and LVIDdN entry thresholds, and focused echo observer variability.

episodes.label: The Cells the Marrow Was Missing — Canine Precursor-Targeted Immune Anemia & Pure Red Cell Aplasia (V020) and Paired Multisite Aspirate vs. Core Biopsy Agreement
episodes.notes: One Medicine veterinary hematopathology (V020): non-regenerative anemia in a puppy with suspected primary pure red cell aplasia (To et al. 2021), canine precursor-targeted immune-mediated anemia (PIMA) rubriphagocytosis and maturation arrest (2023), and paired 2026 multisite humerus-vs.-ilium bone-marrow cytology and core-biopsy reader-agreement studies.

episodes.label: Rabies Beyond the Known Range — Omaha Kitten Eastern Raccoon Variant (V056), DFA vs. Pan-Lyssavirus LN34 RT-qPCR Discordance & Variant Surveillance
episodes.notes: One Medicine zoonotic neurovirology and diagnostic validation (V056): Stein et al.'s (2024 MMWR) detection of Eastern raccoon rabies virus variant in an Omaha stray kitten outside its enzootic range, Gigante et al.'s (2018) multisite LN34 pan-lyssavirus RT-qPCR validation against direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) testing, Dettinger et al.'s (2022) Pennsylvania discordance series, and targeted wildlife surveillance limits.

episodes.label: The Thermostat That Lies Across Species — Human Thyroid Traps, Greyhound Baselines, Occult Feline Hyperthyroidism & Canine Adrenal Dynamics
episodes.notes: One Medicine comparative deep dive (H009, V021, V022, V023): human biotin fake-Graves' storm vs. equilibrium dialysis, healthy Greyhound low basal T4, feline azotemia masking hyperthyroidism, canine Addison's TSH surges & Cushing's LDDST escape, plus Index of Individuality (II ~ 0.35), log-linear TSH-fT4 gain, and RCV math.

episodes.notes: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

episodes.label: The Signal That Outlasted the Cigarette — Exhaled CO vs. Urine Cotinine & Anabasine on Nicotine Patch, Langley's Receptor Concept, Human alpha4-beta2 nAChR Varenicline Cryo-EM (6UR8) & the EAGLES Trial
episodes.notes: From John Newport Langley's 1905 'receptive substance' to transplant tobacco abstinence verification: human alpha4-beta2 nAChR cryo-EM structure bound to varenicline (PDB 6UR8), cytisine-to-varenicline partial agonist design, CYP2A6 nicotine-to-cotinine kinetics, LC-MS/MS separation of isobaric nicotine and minor tobacco alkaloid anabasine (m/z 163), and the 8,144-participant EAGLES trial.

episodes.label: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
episodes.notes: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

episodes.label: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

episodes.label: The Vitamin the Body Couldn't Clear — PTH-Suppressed Hypercalcemia, Human VDR-Calcitriol Structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann's LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D:24,25(OH)2D Ratio & CYP24A1 Loss
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of vitamin D catabolism and CYP24A1 deficiency: why normal 25(OH)D3 with suppressed PTH and elevated 1,25(OH)2D3 points to failed 24-hydroxylase inactivation rather than overdose, the 1.8 Å human VDR-calcitriol crystal structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann & Jones's (2014) PTAD-derivatized LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D3:24,25(OH)2D3 molar ratio diagnostic (>80), and Schlingmann et al.'s (2011) discovery of idiopathic infantile and adult CYP24A1 hypercalcemia.

episodes.label: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

episodes.label: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

episodes.label: The Letter the First Test Missed — Compound Heterozygous DPYD Variants Missed by 4-SNP Panels (de Haar-Holleman 2024), Fluorouracil Catabolism Collapse & Uridine Triacetate Antidote Rescue
episodes.notes: Pharmacogenomics and biochemical rescue of fluoropyrimidine toxicity: why targeted 4-variant DPYD genotyping misses rare in-trans compound heterozygotes (de Haar-Holleman et al. 2024), phenotypic DPD uracil breath/plasma assays (Coenen et al. 2019), 5-FU catabolic shunting into FUTP/FdUMP (Peters et al. 1988), and emergency antidote rescue with uridine triacetate (Jacob et al. 2022).

episodes.label: The Antibody and the Unhealed Colon — Infliximab TNF-Alpha Trimer Crystal Structure (PDB 4G3Y), Transmembrane Avidity, Endoscopic Mucosal Healing (ACT 1/2) & Anti-Drug Antibody Clearance
episodes.notes: Structural immunology and therapeutic drug monitoring of infliximab in ulcerative colitis: chimeric cA2 engineering (Knight 1993), 2.60 Å TNF-alpha:infliximab Fab crystal structure (PDB 4G3Y, Liang 2013), transmembrane TNF bivalent avidity (Scallon 2002), ACT 1 & ACT 2 mucosal healing trials (Rutgeerts 2005), and anti-drug antibody clearance vs. assay non-interchangeability.

episodes.label: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. (2009, 2010) Phase 3 timed 25-foot walk responder denominators (78/224 vs. 6/72; 51/119 vs. 11/118), extended-release vs. oral solution Cmax, and why renal impairment (CrCl <= 50 mL/min) precipitates acute seizures.

episodes.label: The Signal That Tested the Pituitary — Ghrelin & GOAT Discovery, Macimorelin Bound to Human GHSR–Gq (PDB 9V2N), 22-kDa GH Immunoassay & ITT Crossover Agreement
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 78: reverse pharmacology from GHSR1a cloning (Howard et al. 1996) to rat stomach ghrelin isolation (Kojima et al. 1999) and GOAT/MBOAT4 Ser3 octanoylation (Yang 2008; Gutierrez 2008), peptidomimetic macimorelin (JMV1843) bound to human GHSR-Gq at 2.63 Å (PDB 9V2N, Asp99/Arg102/Ser123), 22-kDa IDS-iSYS chemiluminescent GH assay, thorough QTcF crossover (+9.61 ms at 4 h), and 139-pair vs. 140-pair diagnostic agreement against the insulin tolerance test (Garcia et al.).

episodes.label: The Number After the Blood Was Cleared — Pre-Dialysis Lithium Rebound, 7Li Brain MRS Half-Life, Spent-Tank Dialysate Recovery & EXTRIP Cohort Predictions
episodes.notes: Multi-compartment pharmacokinetics and clinical toxicology of lithium clearance: pre-dialysis serum rebound during IV hydration in chronic toxicity with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Kobylianskii et al. 2021, 1.50->0.40->1.30 mmol/L), human 7Li brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy vs. serum half-lives (Plenge et al. 1994), direct mass recovery of 250 mg lithium in collected spent dialysate vs. serum percentage reduction (Schmidt et al. 2014), and retrospective evaluation of EXTRIP dialysis criteria across 361 poisonings (Buckley et al. 2020).

episodes.label: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
episodes.notes: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

episodes.label: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

episodes.label: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 81: neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia critical-sample diagnostics (simultaneous glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and free fatty acids; Ferrara et al.), repurposing antihypertensive benzothiadiazine diazoxide (Drash & Wolff 1964), beta-cell SUR1/Kir6.2 KATP opening and NN414 comparator structure (PDB 7W4O), dominant KCNJ11 p.Phe55Leu gating vs. recessive focal 11p15 loss, and echocardiographic surveillance for diazoxide-associated pulmonary hypertension (Herrera et al., 7/295).

episodes.label: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

episodes.label: How a Blood Test Tracks the Insulin Your Body Makes — Berson & Yalow's 1956–1960 Competitive 131I-Insulin Radioimmunoassay, Melani's 1970 Serum C-Peptide Separation & Modern Two-Antibody Electrochemiluminescence
episodes.notes: How an unexpected antibody artifact became the foundation of clinical endocrinology: Berson & Yalow's (1956-1960) competitive radioimmunoassay (where rising unlabeled hormone lowers the bound-to-free tracer ratio), Melani, Rubenstein & Steiner's (1970) detection of equimolar co-secreted C-peptide in human serum, and modern two-antibody electrochemiluminescent C-peptide testing in insulin-treated patients.

episodes.label: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
episodes.notes: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

episodes.label: How the ECG Learned to Follow You Home — Waller's 1887 Limb Recordings, Einthoven's Calibrated Quartz String Galvanometer, Holter's 1961 Portable Tape Recorder & Barrett's 2014 24-Hour vs. 14-Day Patch Comparison
episodes.notes: From bedside galvanometers to ambulatory rhythm monitoring (H041): Waller's (1887) limb-contact control ruling out mechanical chest movement, Einthoven's (1903) calibrated string galvanometer, Holter's (1961) portable battery-powered recorder, and Barrett et al.'s (2014) paired 146-patient comparison showing why the adhesive patch's diagnostic advantage over 24-hour Holter monitoring (96 vs. 61) came from extended sampling duration rather than Day-1 superiority (52 vs. 61).

episodes.label: How One Breath Tests Gas Transfer — Marie Krogh's 1915 Paired Breath Samples, Ogilvie & Forster's 1957 Helium-Dilution Single-Breath DLCO & Roughton-Forster Membrane vs. Red-Cell Partitioning
episodes.notes: From Marie Krogh's 1915 diffusion experiments to modern single-breath DLCO (H043): paired breath-hold sampling, Ogilvie & Forster's (1957) inert helium tracer dilution separating airspace mixing from true vascular uptake, Roughton & Forster's (1957) serial membrane and erythrocyte resistance model, and clinical interpretation of DLCO, VA, and KCO.

episodes.label: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
episodes.notes: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

episodes.label: How a Treadmill ECG Tests the Heart Under Load — Master's 1929 Two-Step Test, Bellet's 1961 Radio-Telemetry Exercise Recording, Bruce's 1963 Multistage Treadmill Protocol & the Duke Treadmill Score
episodes.notes: From two-step challenges to multistage exercise stress testing (H042): Master & Oppenheimer's (1929) standardized step workload, Bellet et al.'s (1961) radiotelemetry during exercise vs. recovery, Bruce et al.'s (1963) graded multistage treadmill protocol, and Mark et al.'s (1987, 1991) Duke treadmill score integrating exercise time, ST deviation, and symptoms.

episodes.label: How a Sealed Booth Measures the Air Left in Your Lungs — Hutchinson's 1846 Vital Capacity Spirometer, DuBois's 1956 Boyle's-Law Body Plethysmograph & Trapped Emphysematous Gas vs. Helium Dilution
episodes.notes: From Hutchinson's 1846 spirometer to DuBois's 1956 body plethysmograph (H043): why standard spirometry cannot measure residual volume, applying Boyle's pressure-volume law across a closed airway shutter inside a sealed cabin, and why plethysmography captures non-communicating bullae and trapped emphysematous gas missed by single-breath helium dilution (Bedell et al. 1956; O'Donnell et al. 2010).

episodes.label: How a Newborn Hearing Screen Listens for an Answer — Jewett & Williston's 1971 Averaged ABR Waves, David Kemp's 1978 Outer-Hair-Cell Otoacoustic Emissions & Starr's 1996 Auditory Neuropathy Paradox
episodes.notes: Objective physiological hearing screening without behavioral responses: Jewett & Williston's (1971) time-locked signal averaging of microvolt auditory brainstem responses (ABR), David Kemp's (1978) discovery of active cochlear outer-hair-cell otoacoustic emissions (OAE), NICU screening validation (Stevens et al. 1990), and Starr et al.'s (1996) discovery of auditory neuropathy with preserved OAEs and absent ABR.

episodes.label: How a Brain Recording Can Reveal a Response Without Movement — Owen's 2006 Tennis/Navigation fMRI Imagery, Sitt's 2014 EEG Complexity Markers & Claassen (2019) / Bodien (2024) Cognitive Motor Dissociation
episodes.notes: Detecting covert command-following in behaviorally unresponsive brain-injured patients: Owen et al.'s (2006) fMRI mental-imagery paradigm, Sitt et al.'s (2014) quantitative EEG markers in disorders of consciousness, Claassen et al.'s (2019) bedside motor-command EEG classifier identifying cognitive motor dissociation and predicting 1-year functional recovery, and Bodien et al.'s (2024) six-center cohort quantifying both prevalence (25%) and negative-result sensitivity limits.

episodes.label: Why a Pinhole Can Sharpen a Blurry Letter — Snellen's 5-Arcminute Optotypes, Bailey-Lovie LogMAR Charts, Campbell & Gregory's 2 mm Aperture & Eagan's Retinal-Illumination Trap
episodes.notes: Physiological optics of clinical visual acuity and refraction (H051): Snellen's (1862) 5-arcminute optotype standard, Bailey & Lovie's (1976) proportional logMAR chart design, Campbell & Gregory's (1960) tradeoff between geometrical blur circles and diffraction across pupil diameters, Eagan et al.'s (1999) demonstration of pinhole retinal-dimming pseudoworsening in maculopathy, and Donders (1864) / Sankaridurg et al. (2017) on cycloplegic vs. non-cycloplegic refraction.

episodes.label: How a Sleep Study Tells Why Breathing Stopped — Gastaut's 1965 Simultaneous EEG/Airflow/Effort Recording, Sullivan's 1981 Nasal CPAP Pneumatic Splint & PSG vs. Home Testing Denominators
episodes.notes: Historical physiology of polysomnography and sleep-disordered breathing (H044): Gastaut, Tassinari & Duron's (1965–1966) polygraphic separation of obstructive, central, and mixed apneas by comparing airflow against thoracoabdominal effort, Sullivan et al.'s (1981) nasal CPAP pneumatic splint experiment, and the denominator divergence between EEG-verified total sleep time in polysomnography and recording/monitoring time in home sleep apnea testing (Bianchi & Goparaju 2017).

episodes.label: What a Bright Spot on a PET Scan Is Made Of — Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]Deoxyglucose Hexokinase Trap, Reivich & Phelps's 1979 Human [18F]FDG-PET & Kubota's 1992 Macrophage Microautoradiography
episodes.notes: Biochemical basis and diagnostic specificity of [18F]FDG-PET (H022): Sokoloff et al.'s (1977) hexokinase metabolic trapping of 2-deoxyglucose-6-phosphate, Reivich & Phelps's (1979) human positron emission tomography translation, Som et al.'s (1980) oncologic uptake, and Kubota et al.'s (1992) cellular microautoradiography proving why activated macrophages and granulation tissue generate intense FDG avidity indistinguishable from cancer on a single SUV number.

episodes.label: How an Electrode Learned to Measure Glucose — Clark & Lyons's 1962 Enzyme Membrane Electrode, Updike & Hicks's 1967 Dual-Cathode Differential Sensor & Basu's 2013 Interstitial Lag
episodes.notes: Electrochemical and physiological foundations of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM): Clark & Lyons's (1962) enzyme-membrane electrode concept, Updike & Hicks's (1967) dual-cathode active-vs-inactivated polyacrylamide 'enzyme electrode' canceling ambient oxygen drift, subcutaneous interstitial fluid sensing and electroactive drug interference, and Basu et al.'s (2013) human tracer microdialysis proof of physiological capillary-to-interstitial glucose lag.

episodes.label: How a Test Maps Vision Away from Where You're Looking — Goldmann's 1945 Hemispherical Kinetic Bowl, Heijl & Krakau's 1975 Automated Blind-Spot Fixation & 20/20 Chiasmal Hemianopia
episodes.notes: Psychophysics and neuro-ophthalmic anatomy of visual field perimetry: Goldmann's (1945) standardized luminance hemispherical bowl and kinetic target-velocity reaction-time artifact, Heijl & Krakau's (1975) automated computerized static threshold perimetry and blind-spot catch trials, and Ogra et al.'s (2014) proof that optic chiasm compression routinely produces bitemporal visual field loss despite 6/6 (20/20) foveal acuity.

episodes.label: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
episodes.notes: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

episodes.label: Why a Pulse Oximeter Needs a Pulse — Millikan & Wood's Bloodless Ear Zero, Takuo Aoyagi's 1974 Pulsatile AC/DC Ratio, Dyshemoglobin 85% Artifacts & Skin-Pigment Bias
episodes.notes: Optical physics and physiological limitations of pulse oximetry: Millikan (1942) and Wood & Geraci's (1949) pneumatic bloodless-ear zeroing, Takuo Aoyagi's (1974) breakthrough using pulsatile arterial AC/DC absorbance ratios at two wavelengths, two-wavelength degrees-of-freedom failure in carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia, and melanin/low-saturation occult hypoxemia bias (Bickler et al. 2005; Sjoding et al. 2020).

episodes.label: How an Eye Scan Finds Layers with Light — Fercher's 1988 Low-Coherence Eye-Length Interferometry, Huang & Fujimoto's 1991 Retinal OCT & Preperimetric Glaucoma RNFL Loss
episodes.notes: Optical physics and clinical translation of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): why femtosecond light propagation requires interferometric path-length matching rather than direct electronic clock timing, Fercher et al.'s (1988) low-coherence axial eye-length interferometry, Huang, Swanson & Fujimoto's (1991) cross-sectional retinal OCT invention, and Miki et al.'s (2014) longitudinal proof of structural RNFL thinning preceding visual field defects in glaucoma.

episodes.label: What an Ear Test Learns by Changing the Pressure — Terkildsen & Thomsen's 1959 Pressure Sweep, Jerger's 1970 Type A/B/C Curves, Equivalent Canal Volume & Infant 1,000 Hz Probes
episodes.notes: Acoustic immittance physics and developmental biomechanics of tympanometry: Terkildsen & Thomsen's (1959) ear-canal pressure-sweep compliance peak, Jerger's (1970) Type A/B/C diagnostic classification, Mehta et al.'s (2006) equivalent ear-canal volume (Vec) three-way disambiguation of flat Type B traces, and Gellrich et al.'s (2024) myringotomy-validated proof of 1,000 Hz vs. 226 Hz probe tones in young infants.

episodes.label: How a Blood Test Keeps a History of Glucose — Rahbar's 1968 Diabetic Hemoglobin Fraction, Bunn's 1976 59Fe-Transferrin Glycation Kinetics, Red-Cell Age & the ADAG Trial
episodes.notes: Biochemistry and hematologic kinetics of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c): Rahbar's (1968) discovery in diabetic erythrocytes, Bunn et al.'s (1976) 59Fe-transferrin pulse-chase proof of slow non-enzymatic postsynthetic Amadori glycation, Fitzgibbons et al.'s (1976) density-fraction proof of erythrocyte age dependence, and Nathan et al.'s (2008) ADAG calibration.

episodes.label: Why a Visual Signal Can Arrive Late After Sight Improves — Dawson's 1954 Signal Averaging, Halliday's 1972 Pattern-Reversal VEP in Optic Neuritis & Sokol's Dioptric Blur Artifact
episodes.notes: Clinical neurophysiology of pattern-reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP): Dawson's (1954) time-locked signal averaging, Halliday, McDonald & Mushin's (1972) discovery of persistent monocular cortical latency delay after visual acuity recovery in optic neuritis, and Sokol & Moskowitz's (1981) demonstration of refractive blur latency artifacts.

episodes.label: How B12 Testing Separates Supply from Absorption — Castle's 1929 Intrinsic Factor Experiment, Schilling's 1953 Two-Stage Radiotracer Assay, Methylmalonic Acid & Anti-IF Antibodies
episodes.notes: Hematologic and biochemical physiology of vitamin B12 diagnostics: Castle's (1929) sequential extrinsic-plus-intrinsic factor reticulocyte experiments, Schilling's (1953) two-stage radiolabeled urinary absorption test with and without intrinsic factor replacement, and modern three-axis serum cobalamin, methylmalonic acid (MMA), and intrinsic-factor antibody testing.

episodes.label: How Pancreas Tests Separate Secretion from Sample Dilution — Burton's 1960 Secretin-Pancreozymin Challenge, Endoscopic Bicarbonate Crossover, Stool Elastase & Lyophilized Water Correction
episodes.notes: Gastrointestinal physiology and specimen physics of exocrine pancreatic testing: from Bayliss & Starling's (1902) secretin discovery and Burton et al.'s (1960) duodenal secretin-pancreozymin aspiration to endoscopic vs. tube bicarbonate crossover validation (Stevens et al. 2006), fecal elastase immunoassay validation (Löser et al. 1996), and Fischer et al.'s (2001) paired freeze-drying experiment showing 16/151 diarrheal stool samples normalize once corrected for water dilution.

episodes.label: How a Flash Test Separates the Retina’s Responses — Adrian's 1945 Red/Blue Scotopic-Photopic ERG, Dilated-Pupil Control, Miyake's Electronegative CSNB Waveform & ISCEV Standards
episodes.notes: Retinal electrophysiology and clinical waveform dissection: Edgar Adrian's (1945) human corneal-thread ERG separating scotopic and photopic responses across wavelengths with dilated-pupil controls, Miyake et al.'s (1986, N=64) electronegative bright-flash ERG in congenital stationary night blindness (preserved photoreceptor a-wave with reduced ON-bipolar b-wave), and 2022 ISCEV full-field and On-Off ERG standards.

episodes.label: How a Vitamin Can Change a Blood Test’s Result — Green's 1963 Avidin-Biotin Kinetics, Streptavidin Capture Immunoassays, Trambas Spiking/Depletion Controls & Sandwich vs. Competitive Interference
episodes.notes: Biochemical kinetics and clinical laboratory physics of biotin immunoassay interference: Green's (1963) radiotracer measurement of avidin-biotin association/exchange, Bayer & Wilchek's (1974) affinity-capture chemistry, Trambas et al.'s (2018) paired serum biotin-spiking and streptavidin-depletion reversal experiments, and Li et al.'s (2017) human supplementation crossover demonstrating opposite interference directions in sandwich vs. competitive immunoassays.
